```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(pROC)
library(sf)
library(here)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))
options(scipen = 999)

set.seed(1)
```

**DRAFT.** This document restructures the Chinook/steelhead mixed-model analysis
([feather_river_cover_analysis_salmon.Rmd](feather_river_cover_analysis_salmon.Rmd))
into a set of pre-specified competing models. 

## Objective

Test which of several hypotheses about habitat best explains fish presence/absence
in the Feather River mini snorkel data (2001-2002), using AICc to compare a fixed set of
models rather than selecting terms stepwise.

## Approach

- **Response:** presence/absence of the target species in a microhabitat unit
  (one row per `micro_hab_data_tbl_id`). Units where only other species were
  seen are absences of the target species.
- **Predictors:** only variables recorded for every unit, so absences are kept.
  Fish-only variables (`fl_mm`, `dist_to_bottom`, `focal_velocity`) are excluded.
- **Cover:** a single 0/1 variable. Percent cover from the Habitat Accounting
  (HA) cover categories is combined, and a unit has cover if the combined
  percent is at least the threshold (20%). The classification is a standalone
  function, [ha_cover.R](ha_cover.R), so the categories, columns, threshold and
  combination rule can be changed without editing this document.
- **Models:** binomial GLMs fit on identical rows. Models 1-7 are the habitat
  hypotheses. Models 8-10 add redd count, season (month) or sampling design to
  the best of models 1-7.
- **Evaluation:** AICc, delta AICc and Akaike weights; odds ratios for the best
  model; leave-one-site-out cross-validated AUC.
- **Robustness:** the whole set is refit with a survey-event random intercept
  because about 36 units are sampled per survey.

Species: `r params$species_pattern`. Cover threshold: `r params$percent_threshold`%
(categories combined by `r params$cover_method`).

## Data

Mini snorkel data are read from local copies of
[edi.1705.2](https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=edi.1705.2)
in `mini-snorkel-analysis/data-raw`. Redd data are read from `edi-redd/data`
(the EDI package for the redd data, edi.1802.2, was not publicly readable when
this draft was written).

```{r read-data}
fish_raw <- read_csv(here("mini-snorkel-analysis", "data-raw", "microhabitat_observations.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE)
locations_raw <- read_csv(here("mini-snorkel-analysis", "data-raw", "survey_locations.csv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE)
redd_raw <- read_csv(here("edi-redd", "data", "redd_observations.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

### Survey attributes

`survey_locations.csv` has more than one row for some surveys
(`location_table_id`), which differ only in their coordinates. Joining it
directly to the fish data would duplicate every unit at those surveys, so survey
attributes are collapsed to one row per survey. The coordinate variants are kept
in `locations_raw` for matching redds to transects.

```{r survey-attrs}
survey_attrs <- locations_raw |>
  select(-latitude, -longitude, -coordinate_method) |>
  distinct()

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(survey_attrs$location_table_id))

tibble(location_rows = nrow(locations_raw), surveys = nrow(survey_attrs)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rows in survey_locations.csv vs. surveys")
```

### Collapse to one row per microhabitat unit

Fish-level rows are summed to the unit. Counts of other species do not make a
unit a presence for the target species.

```{r unit-level}
unit_vars <- c("location_table_id", "date", "transect_code", "depth", "velocity",
               "surface_turbidity", "channel_geomorphic_unit",
               "percent_small_woody_cover_inchannel", "percent_large_woody_cover_inchannel",
               "percent_submerged_aquatic_veg_inchannel", "percent_undercut_bank",
               "percent_cover_half_meter_overhead", "percent_cover_more_than_half_meter_overhead",
               "percent_boulder_substrate", "percent_cobble_substrate")

# Check that unit-level covariates really are constant within a unit
unit_consistency <- fish_raw |>
  group_by(micro_hab_data_tbl_id) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(unit_vars), n_distinct), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(across(all_of(unit_vars), ~ sum(.x > 1)))
stopifnot(all(unit_consistency == 0))

units <- fish_raw |>
  group_by(micro_hab_data_tbl_id) |>
  summarise(
    target_count = sum(count[str_detect(species, params$species_pattern) & !is.na(species)],
                       na.rm = TRUE),
    across(all_of(unit_vars), first),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(presence = as.integer(target_count > 0)) |>
  left_join(survey_attrs, by = c("location_table_id", "date"))

stopifnot(nrow(units) == n_distinct(fish_raw$micro_hab_data_tbl_id))

units |>
  summarise(units = n(), presences = sum(presence), absences = sum(presence == 0),
            prevalence = round(mean(presence), 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Units and presences of the target species")
```

### Factor coding

```{r coding}
units <- units |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(month(date)),
    channel_location = factor(channel_location),
    channel_geomorphic_unit = factor(channel_geomorphic_unit),
    location = factor(location),
    location_table_id = factor(location_table_id)
  )
```

### Cover: one variable from the HA categories

The Habitat Accounting protocol treats cover as a qualifying criterion for
rearing habitat: if at least 20% of the area includes cover features (habitat
suitability index of at least 0.5), the area counts as rearing habitat
(Appendix F, section 2.1.3.5). The 20% applies to cover features **together**,
not to each type separately. This replaces the earlier approach of five separate
0/1 variables, so the cover hypothesis is a single term and models read as
`cover + depth + velocity + other`.

`classify_ha_cover()` in [ha_cover.R](ha_cover.R) does this:

1. For each HA category, add the percent from its data column(s), capped at 100.
2. Combine the categories (`"sum"` by default, or `"max"`).
3. `cover = 1` if the combined percent is at least the threshold, otherwise 0.
   The continuous combined percent is kept as `cover_pct`.

The mapping from HA categories to mini snorkel columns is `ha_cover_map`:

```{r cover-map}
source(here("mini-snorkel-analysis", "analysis", "ha_cover.R"))

ha_cover_map |>
  group_by(ha_category) |>
  summarise(columns = paste(column, collapse = " + ")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "HA cover categories and the mini snorkel columns used (edit ha_cover_map in ha_cover.R)")
```

The categories are those the State Water Board lists for Table 28 of the
protocol (woody debris, boulder, grass/herbaceous, willow and other riparian
vegetation, undercut bank, aquatic vegetation, overhanging vegetation, root
wad/logjam/large wood). Grass/herbaceous and willow/riparian vegetation have no
matching column in the mini snorkel data. Boulder and cobble are recorded as
substrate in the survey but are counted as cover here (the VA accounting
documents include cobble as cover; the State Water Board's summary of Table 28
does not, so cobble is a choice to confirm). Undercut bank in HA must be at
least 0.5 ft, which the survey did not record.

```{r cover-classify}
# Edit to change which HA categories count as cover, e.g.
# cover_use <- setdiff(unique(ha_cover_map$ha_category), "boulder")
cover_use <- unique(ha_cover_map$ha_category)

units <- classify_ha_cover(units,
                           threshold = params$percent_threshold,
                           use = cover_use,
                           method = params$cover_method,
                           keep_categories = TRUE)

cover_cols <- ha_cover_map$column[ha_cover_map$ha_category %in% cover_use]
```

```{r cover-diagnostics, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 8}
tibble(
  n_units = nrow(units),
  with_cover = sum(units$cover, na.rm = TRUE),
  pct_with_cover = round(100 * mean(units$cover, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  missing_cover = sum(is.na(units$cover))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Units classified as having cover")

units |>
  filter(!is.na(cover)) |>
  group_by(presence = ifelse(presence == 1, "target species present", "absent")) |>
  summarise(units = n(), pct_with_cover = round(100 * mean(cover), 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Share of units with cover, by fish presence (raw, no model)")

units |>
  select(starts_with("ha_") & ends_with("_pct")) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "ha_category", values_to = "pct") |>
  group_by(ha_category) |>
  summarise(pct_units_nonzero = round(100 * mean(pct > 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            mean_pct_when_present = round(mean(pct[pct > 0], na.rm = TRUE), 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "How often each HA category is recorded, and its mean percent when recorded")

units |>
  filter(!is.na(cover_pct)) |>
  ggplot(aes(cover_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = params$percent_threshold, linetype = 2, color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Combined HA cover (%)", y = "Units",
       title = "Combined cover per unit (dashed = threshold)")
```

### Predictor standardization

Continuous predictors are standardized (`_z`, per 1 SD) in the model data so
odds ratios are comparable.

### Redd count

Redds are matched to the nearest mini snorkel transect point within
`r params$redd_max_dist_m` m and summed by transect location. Redd data are
2014-2023 and the snorkel data are 2001-2002, so redd count is a site-level
index of spawning use, not a year-matched value. It is constant within a site.

```{r redd}
site_pts <- locations_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
  distinct(location, latitude, longitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(26910)

redd_pts <- redd_raw |>
  filter(number_redds > 0, !is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(26910)

nearest <- st_nearest_feature(redd_pts, site_pts)

redd_by_site <- redd_pts |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(site = site_pts$location[nearest],
         dist_m = as.numeric(st_distance(redd_pts, site_pts[nearest, ], by_element = TRUE))) |>
  filter(dist_m <= params$redd_max_dist_m) |>
  group_by(location = site) |>
  summarise(redd_total = sum(number_redds), .groups = "drop")

units <- units |>
  left_join(redd_by_site, by = "location") |>
  mutate(redd_total = replace_na(redd_total, 0))

tibble(
  redds_total = sum(redd_pts$number_redds),
  redds_matched = sum(redd_by_site$redd_total),
  sites_with_redds = nrow(redd_by_site),
  sites_total = n_distinct(units$location)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Redds matched to mini snorkel transect locations")
```

### Model data

Complete cases are taken **once**, on the union of variables used by any model,
so every model is fit to the same rows. The table shows what is lost.

```{r model-data}
needed <- c("presence", "location", "location_table_id", "channel_location",
            "channel_geomorphic_unit", "number_of_divers", "month",
            "depth", "velocity", "surface_turbidity", "cover", "cover_pct",
            cover_cols,   # raw percent columns, kept for the cover sensitivity checks
            if (params$use_redd) "redd_total",
            if (params$include_optional) "flow")

missing_summary <- units |>
  select(all_of(needed)) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0)

if (nrow(missing_summary) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(missing_summary, caption = "Units with missing values by variable")
}

zscore <- function(x) as.numeric(scale(x))

model_data <- units |>
  select(all_of(needed)) |>
  drop_na() |>
  droplevels() |>
  mutate(cover_pct_z = zscore(cover_pct),
         depth_z = zscore(depth),
         velocity_z = zscore(velocity),
         surface_turbidity_z = zscore(surface_turbidity),
         redd_z = if (params$use_redd) zscore(redd_total) else NA_real_,
         flow_z = if (params$include_optional) zscore(flow) else NA_real_,
         number_of_divers = factor(number_of_divers))

tibble(step = c("Units", "Complete cases on all model variables"),
       n = c(nrow(units), nrow(model_data)),
       presences = c(sum(units$presence), sum(model_data$presence)),
       absences = c(sum(units$presence == 0), sum(model_data$presence == 0))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rows retained for modeling")
```

## Candidate models

```{r specs}
cover_rhs <- "cover"          # combined HA cover, 0/1
cover_rhs_pct <- "cover_pct_z"  # combined HA cover, continuous (sensitivity)

add_term <- function(rhs, x) if (rhs == "1") x else paste(rhs, "+", x)

stage1_specs <- function(cover_rhs) {
  specs <- tribble(
    ~model,       ~rhs,                                                      ~hypothesis,
    "null",       "1",                                                       "Habitat variables add nothing",
    "cover",      cover_rhs,                                                 "Cover explains occurrence",
    "cover_turb", paste(cover_rhs, "+ surface_turbidity_z"),                 "Cover plus surface turbidity",
    "depth",      "depth_z",                                                 "Depth explains occurrence",
    "flow",       "velocity_z",                                              "Flow (velocity) explains occurrence",
    "dcv",        paste("depth_z + velocity_z +", cover_rhs),                "Depth, cover and velocity combine",
    "dcv_turb",   paste("depth_z + velocity_z +", cover_rhs, "+ surface_turbidity_z"),
                                                                             "Depth, cover, velocity and turbidity combine"
  )
  if (params$include_optional) {
    specs <- bind_rows(
      specs,
      tribble(
        ~model,        ~rhs,                                         ~hypothesis,
        "depth_cover", paste("depth_z +", cover_rhs),                "Depth and cover",
        "depth_vel",   "depth_z + velocity_z",                       "Depth and velocity",
        "cover_vel",   paste("velocity_z +", cover_rhs),             "Cover and velocity",
        "flow_survey", "flow_z",                                     "Survey-level flow explains occurrence"
      )
    )
  }
  specs
}

design_rhs <- "channel_location + channel_geomorphic_unit + number_of_divers"

specs_main <- stage1_specs(cover_rhs)

specs_main |>
  mutate(rhs = str_wrap(rhs, 70)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Stage 1: habitat hypotheses (fit first)")
```

Stage 2 adds one group of terms to whichever stage 1 model has the lowest
AICc:

| Model | Added to the best stage 1 model |
|---|---|
| `best_redd` | redd count (`redd_z`), Chinook only |
| `best_season` | month |
| `best_design` | `r design_rhs` |

## Fitting and comparison

```{r helpers}
aicc_table <- function(models) {
  tibble(
    model = names(models),
    k = map_int(models, ~ as.integer(attr(logLik(.x), "df"))),
    n = map_int(models, nobs),
    logLik = map_dbl(models, ~ as.numeric(logLik(.x)))
  ) |>
    mutate(AICc = -2 * logLik + 2 * k + 2 * k * (k + 1) / (n - k - 1),
           delta_AICc = AICc - min(AICc),
           weight = exp(-delta_AICc / 2) / sum(exp(-delta_AICc / 2))) |>
    arrange(AICc)
}

fit_set <- function(data, specs, random = NULL) {
  fit <- function(rhs) {
    f <- as.formula(paste("presence ~", rhs, if (!is.null(random)) paste("+", random)))
    if (is.null(random)) glm(f, data = data, family = binomial)
    else glmmTMB(f, data = data, family = binomial)
  }
  stage1 <- set_names(map(specs$rhs, fit), specs$model)
  stage1_tab <- aicc_table(stage1)
  best <- stage1_tab$model[1]
  best_rhs <- specs$rhs[specs$model == best]

  stage2_rhs <- c(
    best_redd = if (params$use_redd) add_term(best_rhs, "redd_z"),
    best_season = add_term(best_rhs, "month"),
    best_design = add_term(best_rhs, design_rhs)
  )
  stage2 <- map(stage2_rhs, fit)

  all_models <- c(stage1, stage2)
  list(models = all_models,
       stage1_best = best,
       rhs = c(set_names(specs$rhs, specs$model), stage2_rhs),
       table = aicc_table(all_models) |> mutate(stage = ifelse(model %in% names(stage1), 1, 2)))
}
```

```{r fit-main}
main <- fit_set(model_data, specs_main)

main$table |>
  mutate(across(c(logLik, AICc, delta_AICc), ~ round(.x, 1)), weight = round(weight, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Model ranking by AICc (best stage 1 model: ", main$stage1_best, ")"))
```

```{r aicc-plot, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 8}
main$table |>
  mutate(model = fct_reorder(model, -delta_AICc)) |>
  ggplot(aes(delta_AICc, model, fill = factor(stage))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = 2, color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("1" = "#0072B2", "2" = "#E69F00"),
                    labels = c("1" = "Stage 1: habitat", "2" = "Stage 2: best + X"),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Delta AICc (dashed line = 2)", y = NULL,
       title = "Hypothesis support (smaller delta AICc = better supported)")
```

Models within about 2 delta AICc of the top model are treated as similarly
supported. The null model appears in the table so it is clear whether any
habitat hypothesis beats intercept-only.

With `r sum(model_data$presence)` presences, the largest model fit
(`r main$table$k[which.max(main$table$k)]` parameters) has roughly
`r round(sum(model_data$presence) / max(main$table$k), 1)` events per parameter;
the usual guideline is at least 10.

## Best model

```{r best-effects, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 8}
best_name <- main$table$model[1]
best_model <- main$models[[best_name]]

effects_df <- broom::tidy(best_model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")

effects_df |>
  mutate(term = fct_reorder(term, estimate)) |>
  ggplot(aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Odds ratio (log scale; continuous predictors per 1 SD)", y = NULL,
       title = paste("Effects in the top-ranked model:", best_name))
```

## Predictive performance

AUC is computed with **leave-one-site-out** cross-validation: each site's units
are predicted by a model fit to all the other sites. This replaces in-sample
AUC, which rewards model size and site-specific intercepts. Log loss is the mean
negative log-likelihood of held-out units (lower is better).

```{r cv}
cv_site <- function(rhs, data, group = "location") {
  f <- as.formula(paste("presence ~", rhs))
  pred <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  for (g in unique(data[[group]])) {
    test <- data[[group]] == g
    p <- tryCatch({
      m <- suppressWarnings(glm(f, data = data[!test, ], family = binomial))
      as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = data[test, ], type = "response"))
    }, error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, sum(test)))
    pred[test] <- p
  }
  ok <- !is.na(pred)
  eps <- 1e-6
  p_clip <- pmin(pmax(pred[ok], eps), 1 - eps)
  tibble(
    n_scored = sum(ok),
    auc_cv = as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(data$presence[ok], pred[ok], levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE))),
    log_loss = -mean(data$presence[ok] * log(p_clip) + (1 - data$presence[ok]) * log(1 - p_clip))
  )
}

if (params$cv_models) {
  cv_results <- imap_dfr(main$rhs, ~ cv_site(.x, model_data) |> mutate(model = .y)) |>
    left_join(main$table |> select(model, AICc, delta_AICc), by = "model") |>
    arrange(AICc) |>
    mutate(across(c(auc_cv, log_loss, AICc, delta_AICc), ~ round(.x, 3)))

  knitr::kable(cv_results, caption = "Leave-one-site-out cross-validation, ordered by AICc")
}
```

Read the cross-validated AUC against the null model's value, not against 0.5.
When a site is held out, an intercept-only model predicts the prevalence of the
other sites, so its pooled predictions are partly anti-correlated with presence
and its pooled AUC falls below 0.5. Log loss does not have this problem and is
the better column for comparing models.

### Confusion matrix of the top model

Presences are rare, so the threshold is set to the observed prevalence rather
than 0.5.

```{r confusion}
best_pred <- predict(best_model, type = "response")
thr <- mean(model_data$presence)
conf <- table(Predicted = as.integer(best_pred > thr), Observed = model_data$presence)
conf

tibble(threshold = round(thr, 3),
       sensitivity = round(conf["1", "1"] / sum(conf[, "1"]), 3),
       specificity = round(conf["0", "0"] / sum(conf[, "0"]), 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "In-sample classification at the prevalence threshold")
```

## Robustness checks

### Survey-event random intercept

About 36 units are sampled per survey (`location_table_id`) and are not
independent. The whole set is refit with `(1 | location_table_id)` in every
model, including the null. If the ranking is similar, conclusions do not depend
on ignoring the clustering.

```{r robust-re}
robust_re <- fit_set(model_data, specs_main, random = "(1 | location_table_id)")

robust_re$table |>
  select(model, stage, k, AICc, delta_AICc, weight) |>
  mutate(across(c(AICc, delta_AICc), ~ round(.x, 1)), weight = round(weight, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Ranking with a survey-event random intercept (best stage 1 model: ",
                                robust_re$stage1_best, ")"))
```

```{r rank-compare}
left_join(
  main$table |> transmute(model, rank_glm = row_number()),
  robust_re$table |> transmute(model, rank_re = row_number()),
  by = "model"
) |>
  arrange(rank_glm) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model rank without and with the survey-event random intercept")
```

### Cover definition

The 20% threshold, the "sum" rule and the choice of categories are all
assumptions. Two checks follow. They are for judging how much the conclusions
depend on those choices, **not** for choosing the best-fitting definition:
picking the cover definition by AICc would add another selection step.

**Threshold, combination rule and categories.** The same rows are refit with
`classify_ha_cover()` under different settings. "sum" adds the categories (no
overlap assumed); "max" uses the largest single category (full overlap
assumed). The true value lies between them. "no_boulder" and "no_cobble" drop
those categories, which the earlier analysis treated as substrate rather than
cover.

```{r cover-grid}
cover_grid <- expand_grid(threshold = c(10, 20, 30),
                          method = c("sum", "max"),
                          categories = c("all", "no_boulder", "no_cobble", "no_boulder_cobble")) |>
  mutate(use = map(categories, ~ switch(.x,
                                         all = cover_use,
                                         no_boulder = setdiff(cover_use, "boulder"),
                                         no_cobble = setdiff(cover_use, "cobble"),
                                         no_boulder_cobble = setdiff(cover_use, c("boulder", "cobble"))))) |>
  distinct(threshold, method, use, .keep_all = TRUE)

cover_sens <- pmap_dfr(cover_grid, function(threshold, method, categories, use) {
  d <- classify_ha_cover(model_data, threshold = threshold, use = use, method = method)
  m <- list(
    null = glm(presence ~ 1, data = d, family = binomial),
    cover = glm(presence ~ cover, data = d, family = binomial),
    dcv = glm(presence ~ cover + depth_z + velocity_z, data = d, family = binomial)
  )
  tab <- aicc_table(m)
  tibble(threshold, method, categories,
         pct_units_with_cover = round(100 * mean(d$cover), 1),
         cover_odds_ratio = round(exp(coef(m$cover)[["cover"]]), 2),
         dAICc_cover_vs_null = round(tab$AICc[tab$model == "null"] - tab$AICc[tab$model == "cover"], 1),
         AICc_dcv = tab$AICc[tab$model == "dcv"])
}) |>
  mutate(AICc_dcv = round(AICc_dcv - min(AICc_dcv), 1)) |>
  rename(dAICc_dcv_vs_best_def = AICc_dcv)

knitr::kable(cover_sens,
             caption = "Cover definition sensitivity (dAICc_cover_vs_null > 0 means the cover-only model beats the null; dAICc_dcv_vs_best_def is relative to the best row of this table)")
```

**Continuous cover.** The combined percent is used as a continuous predictor
(`cover_pct_z`) in place of the 0/1 variable:

```{r robust-cont}
specs_cont <- stage1_specs(cover_rhs_pct)
sens_cont <- fit_set(model_data, specs_cont)

sens_cont$table |>
  select(model, stage, k, AICc, delta_AICc, weight) |>
  mutate(across(c(AICc, delta_AICc), ~ round(.x, 1)), weight = round(weight, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Ranking with continuous cover percentages (best stage 1 model: ",
                                sens_cont$stage1_best, ")"))
```

## Caveats

- Redd count is a site-level constant from different years than the snorkel
  surveys, so `best_redd` cannot be separated from site differences.
- Survey-level flow (optional) is tied to channel and month and may act as a
  proxy for sampling design or season.
- Choosing the best of stage 1 and then adding terms is a selection step.
  Check whether stage 1 has near-ties before interpreting stage 2.
- Complete cases are taken on the union of variables so AICc is valid; models
  with fewer variables therefore lose units with missing velocity.
- HA applies the 20% criterion to the share of an area (that already meets
  depth and velocity criteria) covered by cover features, with an optional
  3-foot buffer around features. Here the share is the combined percent
  recorded for a microhabitat unit, and no buffer is applied.
- Percent cover in the data is recorded in separate in-channel and overhead
  layers that can overlap in space. "sum" can overstate combined cover and
  "max" can understate it; the cover definition checks show how much this
  matters.
- Two HA cover categories (grass/herbaceous, willow and other riparian
  vegetation) are not measured, and the 0.5 ft minimum for undercut banks is
  not recorded. Overhanging vegetation is the closest proxy for riparian
  cover.
- The HA categories come from the State Water Board's summary of Table 28 of
  the Habitat Accounting Protocols. The table itself was not available when
  this was written; check `ha_cover_map` against the final protocol.
- Surface turbidity is zero for most units and may be driven by a few survey
  days.
- Presence/absence in a snorkel unit reflects detection as well as habitat use.
  Visibility (turbidity) and number of divers may affect detection.
